headline: The GH support stack
punch: Every entry graded by what the evidence actually is.

headline: Why anything else is needed
body: High-dose GH has two documented costs and they are different in kind. One is metabolic: fasting insulin **P = 0.011** and C-peptide **P = 0.019** rose on the high arm in Mauras. | The other is thyroid: free T4 falls because GH accelerates its conversion into T3, while GH simultaneously blunts the TSH you would screen with. Everything in this stack exists to close one of those two leaks.

headline: T4
body: This is the best-supported adjunct on the list and it is not close. GH upregulates type 2 deiodinase, **free T4 declines significantly** by about 1.09 pmol/L, and GH blunts TSH pulsatility so the routine screen misses it. | In hypopituitary adults, GH replacement unmasked central hypothyroidism in **36 to 47%** of patients who looked euthyroid before starting. Up to half.
punch: ==Mechanism documented, incidence measured. Screen free T4.==

headline: T3
body: Separate from T4 and a weaker case. GH already raises free T3 by accelerating conversion, so in most people on GH the T3 side is being pushed up rather than down. | Adding T3 on top addresses a problem the drug is already solving in one direction while draining the substrate in the other. The deficit is in T4 supply, so T4 is the rational replacement. T3 is for a measured low T3 after T4 is adequate, not a default.
punch: The deficit is T4. Replace the thing that is falling.

headline: Empagliflozin
body: An SGLT2 inhibitor. It lowers glucose by increasing urinary glucose excretion, independently of insulin, which is why it does not carry insulin's hypoglycaemia profile. | It targets exactly the axis GH drifts: glucose handling and insulin sensitivity. Evidence grade, stated plainly: an established agent for that target, with **no trial testing it alongside GH for this purpose**. Mechanism sound, combination untested.

headline: Imeglimin
body: Works on mitochondrial function in the beta cell and on peripheral insulin sensitivity, which is a different mechanism from the SGLT2 route and in principle complementary rather than redundant. | Same evidence grade as above and it needs saying every time: established for its own indication, **never tested with GH**. Two untested-in-combination agents stacked together is two inferences, not one.

headline: Exogenous insulin
subhead: DOWNSIDE · WHY IT IS NOT ON THIS LIST
body: The one adjunct I will not put in the stack, and the reason is specific rather than squeamish. Insulin does not improve insulin sensitivity. It adds insulin to a system whose problem is that it has stopped responding to insulin. | The whole human IGF-1 evidence base for insulin is people who were **deficient** having it **restored**. Nobody has shown that adding insulin to a working pancreas moves IGF-1 or height.
punch: Resistance is not treated by adding more of the hormone.

headline: The specific hazard
body: Holding blood glucose at **4.5 to 5.5 mmol/L** with exogenous insulin in someone with a working pancreas is targeting the bottom of the normal band with a drug the literature describes as having **a narrow therapeutic window**. | A 30-year-old using insulin to stimulate GH convulsed, required intubation, and glucose infusion alone was not enough to stabilise him. It took glucagon in intensive care. That was short-acting insulin.
punch: ==A tight target with a drug that overshoots is the failure mode.==

headline: What to do instead
body: The goal behind that idea is correct: keep glucose handling tight so GH-induced insulin resistance does not accumulate. The sensitivity agents above reach the same target without adding an unopposed glucose-lowering drug. | Keeping carbohydrate away from the bedtime GH dose does double duty, since a pre-bed carbohydrate load also flattens the nocturnal slow-wave-sleep GH surge.
punch: Same goal. Reached from the sensitivity side.

headline: What to actually measure
body: **Free T4** and free T3, not TSH, because TSH is the parameter GH suppresses. **Fasting insulin** and HbA1c, because those are the markers that moved in the trial. And **IGF-1 against the 2 SDS ceiling**, since 28% of the high-dose arm overshot it. | That set covers both leaks and every item on it moved measurably in a published trial.
punch: Free T4, fasting insulin, IGF-1 SDS.

headline: The honest grading
body: T4 is documented mechanism plus measured incidence. The sensitivity agents are sound mechanism against a documented GH cost, with no combination trial behind them. | None of this stack has been tested as a stack, in anyone, for this purpose. That does not make it wrong. It means the grade is mechanism-level and should be labelled as mechanism-level rather than borrowed from the GH trials.
punch: _One tier of evidence for T4. A lower tier for the rest._

headline: Verdict
body: T4 is close to mandatory on high-dose GH and it is the entry with real numbers behind it. The insulin sensitivity side is a real target with reasonable agents and no combination evidence. | And the one thing to leave out is exogenous insulin, because it treats the wrong variable and its failure mode is unforgiving in a way nothing else here is.
punch: Replace T4. Protect sensitivity. Do not add insulin.
